chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in praying upon all the statues if you place them beneath you."

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلِ: Statues or images of living beings
key_terms.تَحْتَكَ: Beneath you (referring to the prayer surface)

ai.seo_question: Does having images of statues on a prayer mat invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the presence of statues (tamyathil) on a prayer surface does not invalidate salat, provided they are positioned beneath the worshipper rather than being directly faced or elevated. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly distinction between the prohibition of prostrating directly to idols and the permissibility of using common materials adorned with images for general prayer, emphasizing the location of the image relative to the body. It underscores the principle that minor decorative elements do not constitute shirk or impurity in the context of valid worship spaces.
